scenes.name: Crunk y trap en Atlanta
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Lil Jon, A&R de So So Def, se convirtió con los East Side Boyz en la cara del crunk (Get Crunk, Who U Wit, 1997). En 1999 Def Jam ya no pudo ignorar el Sur y creó Def Jam South con Scarface al frente, que fichó a Chris Lova Lova, DJ de Hot 97.5 que vendía Incognegro desde el maletero: Ludacris (Back for the First Time, 2000). T.I., tras fracasar en Arista, se hizo fuerte con las mixtapes de DJ Drama, fundó Grand Hustle y con Trap Muzik (2003) llevó al gran público el trap, la música de la calle del trapicheo: sintetizadores, baterías potentes y charles nerviosos, con productores como DJ Toomp, Shawty Redd, Drumma Boy, Lex Luger o Zaytoven, cuyo piano hizo brillar a Gucci Mane (en un solo día de 2009 salieron «Bricks» y «Make Tha Trap Say Aye»). Luego Jeezy, Future, Migos, 21 Savage o Lil Baby: Atlanta, ciudad del fénix, destruye su sonido cada pocos años para crear otro.

scenes.name: El fin del sampleo libre y el oficio del productor
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Transformar lo que existía en algo nuevo está en la base del hip hop: de los breaks de los pioneros a la caja de Marley Marl, el muro de la Bomb Squad y los collages de jazz de De La Soul, Tribe, Pete Rock o DJ Premier. Nadie pensaba en derechos hasta que el rap dio dinero. En diciembre de 1991 Gilbert O’Sullivan ganó a Biz Markie por samplear «Alone Again (Naturally)» sin permiso (250.000 dólares y la retirada del disco); De La Soul pactó con los Turtles. Biz llamó a su siguiente disco All Samples Cleared! y el salvaje Oeste se acabó: a los productores de Rush les dieron una lista de artistas intocables, y Easy Mo Bee empezó a samplear instrumentos sueltos y tocar encima («Flava in Ya Ear»). «La cultura negra siempre recibe las sobras y las convierte en lo que lo controla todo» (Salaam Remi). El productor es también psiquiatra y entrenador; hoy se hace un éxito con un portátil, y algunos, como Timbaland regalándole su archivo de sonidos a Just Blaze, rompieron la costumbre de tapar las etiquetas.

scenes.name: Grammys, Óscars, Hall of Fame y el Pulitzer
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Los grandes premios rechazaron o reconocieron tarde al hip hop. En los Grammy de 1984, la noche de Thriller, Herbie Hancock tocó «Rockit» con Grand Mixer D.ST en los platos: para Paradise Gray, la primera vez que se vio en la tele. En 1989 se creó el Grammy al mejor rap pero se entregó fuera de la retransmisión: Def Jam y Rush encabezaron el boicot y DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince no fueron a recoger el premio por «Parents Just Don’t Understand»; Kool Moe Dee sí fue, harto de que nadie hablara de estrategia («¿no decíamos que nos importaba un carajo el Grammy?»). En 1990 Young MC lo ganó en directo a «Fight the Power» y Flavor Flav le asaltó el escenario. Eminem fue el primer rapero en ganar un Óscar con «Lose Yourself» (2003, con Luis Resto), y Three 6 Mafia el segundo; Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five entraron los primeros en el Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2007). En 2014 Macklemore se disculpó con Kendrick Lamar por ganarle; en 2018 DAMN. de Lamar, criado en Top Dawg por Punch, ganó el Pulitzer, algo que Nation of Millions habría merecido treinta años antes.

scenes.name: Escribir rimas: libretas, cabezas y negros
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Desde Rakim, KRS-One y Kane, la lírica es un arte competitivo: unos escriben en libretas, otros en el móvil en un atasco, otros, como Biggie, Jay-Z o Styles P, en la cabeza. Para unos hay que «dejar joyas» y enseñar (Chuck D: «no rimo por rimar»); para otros basta con que suene bien sobre la base. Cormega tira nueve de cada diez rimas; K-Rino dice que el bloqueo es falta de lecturas; Bruce Lee y las diez mil horas. El negro (ghostwriting) existe desde que Caz rapeó sin saberlo en «Rapper’s Delight»: Kane escribía para la Juice Crew, The D.O.C. y Eminem para Dr. Dre, y Meek Mill acusó a Drake; para unos traiciona la autenticidad, para otros es como Al Pacino haciendo de cubano.

scenes.name: El hip hop: medio siglo de historia oral
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Un género nacido de la imaginación de chavales abandonados entre las ruinas del Bronx de los setenta que sobrevivió a todo (a una generación mayor que lo rechazaba, a las radios que no lo ponían, a los políticos que lo atacaban) hasta convertirse en la música más popular de Estados Unidos. Abrams hizo más de trescientas entrevistas entre 2018 y 2022 a DJs, artistas, productores, ejecutivos y periodistas para contar su origen y su expansión: del Bronx a los demás distritos «como las venas de un plano del metro», del parque al vinilo, a la Costa Oeste con el gangsta rap y el G-funk, al Sur y más allá. «La lírica es, al fin y al cabo, una forma de tradición oral.»

facts.body: Radiohead did not perform in Toronto again until July 19, 2018, six years after the fatal stage collapse. facts.title: Wanda Richardson's Public Statement (2018)
facts.body: Jeremy Dell's mother, Wanda Richardson, gave her first public interview about her son's death to a local ABC affiliate, WFAA, in 2018. She stated that "That day that he died did not define his life," emphasizing his identity as a son, brother, nephew, cousin, grandson, friend, and talented individual. Initially in shock and disbelief, she later reflected on how she thinks of other mothers and sisters affected by school shootings, wanting to comfort them, although she still isn't sure of the exact "why" behind her son's actions. "That day that he died did not define his life."

facts.title: Pyeongchang 2018 Winter Olympics "Scam Trip"
facts.body: The band "drifted" into performing at the Canada House during the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics. The opportunity arose after they jokingly tweeted to Art Canada and Canada House (who were using "Knockin' at the Door" as a theme song) about covering their expenses for a trip. Within three days, they were on a plane, flying coach for a 14.5-hour flight without bringing instruments due to last-minute arrangements. They played three house-party style shows over the last five days of the Olympics, largely for athletes who were "ready to party" having finished their events, playing on the ground because the stage was only big enough for drums. "Yeah, that's a 14 and a half hour flight. Yeah. Did they, at least spring for premium economy? No, we were absolutely not. We were in coach."

facts.title: Death at London Hilton (January 15, 2018)
facts.body: Dolores O'Riordan died in room 2005 at the London Hilton on Park Lane in Mayfair on January 15, 2018. She had flown from New York to London to work on a solo project titled "Dark" and discuss a new Cranberries album. At 1:12 am, she left an enthusiastic voicemail for a friend about the recording progress, and at 2:00 am, she called her mother, with things appearing fine. She was later found submerged in her bathtub, with numerous empty mini-bar alcohol bottles, an empty champagne bottle, and prescription pills in the room. Toxicology reports indicated that drugs were not an issue, but her blood alcohol content at the time of death was 0.33, more than four times the legal limit for drunk driving. Her death was ruled as accidental drowning due to alcohol toxicity. She was 46. "Dolores or Reardon of the Cranberries... found her submerged in the bathtub."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: Last Communications (January 14-15, 2018)
facts.body: On Sunday, January 14, 2018, she emailed The Cranberries guitarist, Noel Hogan, sketches of new songs. facts.title: Discovery and Official Report (January 15, 2018 - September 16, 2018)
facts.body: Dolores O'Riordan was discovered at approximately 9 AM on January 15, 2018, by a maid who came to tidy the room, found face up in the tub with water covering her mouth and nose. Police were called, CPR was performed, but she was declared dead at 9:16 AM at the age of 46. The final report on her death, released on September 16, 2018 (which would have been her 47th birthday), concluded that she died from accidental drowning due to alcohol intoxication, with no suicide note found and rumors of fentanyl involvement disproven. "She was found at about 9 in the morning of January 15th by a maid who had come to tidy up. She was face up in the tub with the water covering her mouth and nose."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.body: Released in December 2018, this song quickly became established across social media as the official soundtrack for the "Yeehaw Agenda." Its initial official music video was composed entirely of Red Dead Redemption 2 game footage. TikTok users found the song especially effective for short cowboy-themed videos, particularly keying into the moment after the opening chorus when the trap beat drops and the lyric "I got the horses in the back" is sung. This track changed the landscape of TikTok, becoming the first hit song plus meme incubated on the platform, following examples like I Love Friday's "Mia Khalifa" which took off as a meme but never charted. The song later scaled charts, tangled with Nashville, and set all-time Hot 100 records. "Old Town Road did what no hit had ever done before."

facts.body: This song propelled Montero Lamar Hill, known as Lil Nas X, to global fame after he independently released it on SoundCloud and iTunes using a beat bought online from producer Young Kio for $30. It gained traction through the "Yeehaw Challenge" meme, quickly rose on the Billboard charts, and secured him a deal with Columbia Records, ultimately selling 18 million copies worldwide, garnering 1.5 billion YouTube views, and over 3 billion streams. Its beat originated from a sample of Nine Inch Nails' instrumental "34 Ghosts 4," leading to Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross receiving songwriting credits. "Montero wrapped over the beats and released it independently on SoundCloud and iTunes."

facts.body: This song was created by rapper Montero Hill (Lil Nas X), who, being "desperate" and seeing it as his "last shot," purchased a remix of Nine Inch Nails' "34 Ghosts 4" from Dutch beatmaker YoungKio. He wrote lyrics over it in about a day and released it independently on December 3, 2018. The song exploded thanks to YouTube and TikTok, especially after Billy Ray Cyrus got involved. It hit number one worldwide and spent a record 19 weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100, making Lil Nas X an international superstar. Due to commercial use of the Creative Commons-licensed "34 Ghosts 4," Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross received official songwriting credits and shared the song's chart records. "The song was Old Town Road. It hit number one of the charts around the world, spending a record 19 weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100."

facts.title: First TikTok Incubated #1 Hit
facts.body: Released in December 2018, this song quickly became established across social media as the official soundtrack for the "Yeehaw Agenda." Its initial official music video was composed entirely of Red Dead Redemption 2 game footage. TikTok users found the song especially effective for short cowboy-themed videos, particularly keying into the moment after the opening chorus when the trap beat drops and the lyric "I got the horses in the back" is sung. This track changed the landscape of TikTok, becoming the first hit song plus meme incubated on the platform, following examples like I Love Friday's "Mia Khalifa" which took off as a meme but never charted. The song later scaled charts, tangled with Nashville, and set all-time Hot 100 records. "Old Town Road did what no hit had ever done before."
